e4ccc699ba746e39.answer: {"subreddit":"MaliciousCompliance","title":"My Manager Oversold The Show. I Counted Every Seat.","script":"My manager sold 40 extra tickets, then ordered me to “find space” without issuing refunds. I worked the lobby at a small comedy club, and the fire-code chart behind the desk showed exactly 120 legal seats. He kept pointing at empty aisles like chairs could magically appear there. So I followed his instruction literally. I found space by measuring every approved seat, checking every reservation, and placing the 40 oversold guests in a neat line beside his office. Then I handed each person a printed receipt showing who authorized the sale. The crowd grew louder while he tried to blame the ticket system. Right then, the venue owner arrived for the opening act. I showed her the fire-code chart, the receipts, and his message telling me to squeeze people in. She refunded every extra ticket from his event bonus and promoted me to front-desk lead before the first joke landed.","hashtags":["MaliciousCompliance","workplace","karma","storytime"],"shots":[{"phrase":"40 extra tickets","query":"ticket counter"},{"phrase":"fire-code chart","query":"venue seating"},{"phrase":"empty aisles","query":"theater aisle"},{"phrase":"printed receipt","query":"paper receipt"},{"phrase":"venue owner","query":"office manager"},{"phrase":"event bonus","query":"payroll document"}],"punches":[{"phrase":"40 extra tickets","text":"OVERSOLD","color":"#ff3030"},{"phrase":"fire-code chart","text":"120 SEATS","color":"#ffaa30"},{"phrase":"promoted me","text":"PROMOTED","color":"#50ff80"}],"music_vibe":"cinematic"}

999203f0ed8a817c.answer: {"subreddit":"TalesFromTheCustomer","title":"The Free Upgrade Cost Him The Entire Order","script":"A customer slammed his iced drink on the counter and demanded the “free premium upgrade” he claimed another cafe promised him. I explained that our tiny shop had no such offer, but he kept filming me and shouting that I was hiding the good menu. My manager whispered, “Give him exactly what he asked for,” then disappeared into the back. So I upgraded everything: the largest cup, double espresso, specialty foam, extra syrup, and the imported topping he pointed at. I placed the finished drink beside an itemized receipt. His grin vanished when the total hit 18 dollars. He argued that “upgrade” meant free, so I replayed his own video where he clearly said, “Charge whatever it costs.” The customers behind him laughed. He paid, took one sip, and quietly asked for a lid. My manager returned just in time to stamp his loyalty card: 1 purchase, 9 more to go.","hashtags":["TalesFromTheCustomer","workplace","karma","storytime"],"shots":[{"phrase":"slammed his iced drink","query":"iced coffee"},{"phrase":"kept filming me","query":"phone recording"},{"phrase":"upgraded everything","query":"coffee toppings"},{"phrase":"itemized receipt","query":"receipt closeup"},{"phrase":"18 dollars","query":"payment terminal"},{"phrase":"loyalty card","query":"stamp card"}],"punches":[{"phrase":"free premium upgrade","text":"FREE?","color":"#ffaa30"},{"phrase":"18 dollars","text":"$18","color":"#ff3030"},{"phrase":"quietly asked","text":"QUIET NOW","color":"#50ff80"}],"music_vibe":"hiphop"}

I told her I was waiting for a rehearsal next door, not working there, but she snapped, “Then find someone who does.” The actual cashier was helping a long line, so the woman followed me through every aisle, demanding a refund for an item from a different store. Finally, she threatened to report me for ignoring customers. I smiled, walked to the service desk, and handed the cashier the box along with the woman’s loud complaint. The barcode scan beeped red: wrong retailer, opened package, no receipt. The woman pointed at my costume again. That was when the rehearsal director entered with 12 actors wearing the exact same outfit. The cashier asked whether she planned to report the entire cast. f90ec6a8a45a6832.answer: {"subreddit":"MaliciousCompliance","title":"The Deleted Recordings Exposed My Manager's Promise","script":"My manager promised every customer their saved recordings would survive our service change, then ordered me to stop mentioning the deletion deadline. I read the approved script word for word, including the line promising “no interruption,” while displaying his email beside it. Customers immediately asked him to sign that promise. He refused. One customer happened to be the regional auditor, who requested the same policy document I had flagged.
